name: Cytokines
summary: Who makes each cytokine and what it does, one row each. “Hot T-bone stEAK”: IL-1 fever (hot), IL-2 T cells, IL-3 bone marrow, IL-4 IgE, IL-5 IgA (and eosinophils), IL-6 aKute-phase proteins. Macrophages make the inflammatory ones (IL-1, IL-6, IL-8, IL-12, TNF-α); Th1 cells IFN-γ; Th2 cells IL-4, IL-5, IL-10, IL-13; Tregs IL-10 and TGF-β.
tissue: everywhere: made locally, many act at a distance

t0.name: Hypothalamus: fever
t0.notes: Hypothalamus: fever. Also endothelium (adhesion molecules) and osteoclasts.

t1.name: T cells and NK cells
t1.notes: Helper, cytotoxic and regulatory T cells and NK cells grow and activate.

t2.name: Bone marrow
t2.notes: Bone marrow stem cells grow and differentiate.

t3.name: B cells: IgE, IgG
t3.notes: B cells switch to IgE and IgG; naive T cells become Th2.

t4.name: Eosinophils; IgA
t4.notes: Eosinophils grow and activate; B cells switch to IgA.

t5.name: Liver: acute phase
t5.notes: Liver makes acute-phase proteins (CRP, fibrinogen, hepcidin); also fever.

t7.name: Th1 cells, macrophages
t7.notes: Th1 cells and activated macrophages are switched off.

t8.name: Th0 → Th1; NK cells
aliases: naive T cells and NK cells
t8.notes: Naive T cells become Th1; NK cells activate.

t9.name: B cells: IgE
t9.notes: B cells switch to IgE; airways make mucus.

t10.name: Macrophages: activated
t10.notes: Macrophages activate: kill intracellular microbes, more MHC, granulomas.

t11.name: Endothelium: shock
t11.notes: Endothelium leaks (septic shock); also cachexia and fever.

il1.name: IL-1
il1.notes: Fever (endogenous pyrogen) and acute inflammation; turns on endothelial adhesion molecules; activates osteoclasts. Anakinra blocks its receptor. “Hot”: IL-1, fever.

il2.name: IL-2
il2.notes: Growth of helper, cytotoxic and regulatory T cells and NK cells. Aldesleukin (recombinant IL-2) treats melanoma and renal cell carcinoma; tacrolimus and cyclosporine block its production (calcineurin); basiliximab blocks its receptor (CD25).

il3.name: IL-3
il3.notes: Like GM-CSF: growth and differentiation of bone marrow stem cells. “Bone”: IL-3, bone marrow.

il4.name: IL-4
il4.notes: Class switching to IgE and IgG; makes naive T cells Th2; ↑ MHC II on B cells. Dupilumab blocks its receptor (atopic dermatitis, asthma). “stEak”: IL-4, IgE.

il5.name: IL-5
il5.notes: Eosinophil growth, differentiation and activation; class switching to IgA. Mepolizumab and reslizumab block it (eosinophilic asthma). “steAk”: IL-5, IgA.

il6.name: IL-6
il6.notes: Acute-phase proteins from the liver (CRP, fibrinogen, hepcidin, ferritin, serum amyloid A) and fever. Tocilizumab blocks its receptor. “steaK”: IL-6, aKute phase.

il8.name: IL-8
il8.notes: The major neutrophil chemokine (CXCL8). “Clean up on aisle 8”: neutrophils clear the area.

il10.name: IL-10
il10.notes: Anti-inflammatory: lowers MHC II and Th1 cytokines, inhibits activated macrophages and dendritic cells. Made by Tregs, Th2 cells and macrophages. (TGF-β also tones things down.)

il12.name: IL-12
il12.notes: Makes naive T cells Th1 and activates NK cells. IL-12 receptor deficiency: disseminated mycobacterial and Salmonella infections. Ustekinumab blocks IL-12 and IL-23 (psoriasis, Crohn disease).

il13.name: IL-13
il13.notes: Like IL-4: IgE class switching; also mucus and airway hyperreactivity in asthma.

ifng.name: IFN-γ
ifng.notes: Activates macrophages (killing of intracellular microbes, granuloma formation), ↑ MHC I and II and antigen presentation in all cells, IgG switching; inhibits Th2. The IFN-γ release assay (QuantiFERON) tests for latent TB.

tnfa.name: TNF-α
tnfa.notes: Endothelial activation and vascular leak (septic shock), cachexia, fever; keeps granulomas intact. Infliximab, adalimumab and etanercept block it (rheumatoid arthritis, IBD, psoriasis); screen for latent TB first, since granulomas can fall apart.
